title: Apple and Cinnamon Porridge
description: Soft oats and grated apple make a warming breakfast with a little crunch from toasted walnuts.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry saucepan over medium heat for 2 minutes, then set aside.
Add the oats, oat milk, grated apple and cinnamon to the saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 8 minutes, stirring frequently, until the oats are soft; add a splash of water if needed.
Divide between two bowls and top with the walnuts and maple syrup.

title: Spinach and Feta Scrambled Eggs
description: Tender eggs, wilted spinach and salty feta turn a slice of toast into a satisfying breakfast.
ingredients: 40 g feta made with vegetarian rennet, crumbled
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk and a few grinds of black pepper.
Warm the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and wilt the spinach for 2 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low, add the eggs and gently fold with a spatula for 3 to 4 minutes until set and no liquid egg remains.
Toast the bread while the eggs cook, then spoon the eggs onto the toast and scatter over the feta.

title: Berry Yogurt Bowl
description: Thick yogurt, juicy berries and crisp oats make a fresh breakfast that needs no cooking.
steps: Wash the berries, remove the strawberry stalks and slice the strawberries.
Divide the yogurt between two bowls and arrange the berries on top.
Scatter over the toasted oats and pumpkin seeds, drizzle with honey and serve immediately.

title: Chickpea and Lemon Salad
description: Chickpeas, cucumber and tomatoes take on a bright lemon dressing in this easy lunch.
ingredients: 1 x 400 g tin chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and black pepper in a large bowl.
Add the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes and onion, then toss gently to coat.
Fold in the parsley, taste for seasoning and divide between two plates.

title: Roasted Tomato Soup
description: Roasting brings sweetness to tomatoes before they are blended into a smooth basil soup.
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the tomatoes, onion and garlic in a roasting tray and toss with the oil and a pinch of salt.
Roast for 30 minutes until the tomatoes soften and begin to brown at the edges.
Tip the vegetables and tray juices into a saucepan, add the stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove from the heat, add the basil and carefully blend with a stick blender until smooth; season and serve.

title: Tuna and White Bean Wraps
description: Tuna and creamy white beans fill soft wraps with crisp lettuce and a tangy yogurt dressing.
ingredients: 1 x 145 g tin tuna in spring water, drained
1 x 400 g tin cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Mash half the beans in a bowl, leaving the remaining beans whole for texture.
Fold in the tuna, yogurt, lemon juice, celery and black pepper.
Lay lettuce on each tortilla, divide the filling between them and roll tightly, tucking in the ends.

title: Lemon Chicken Traybake
description: Chicken thighs roast over potatoes and carrots with lemon and thyme for a simple family dinner.
ingredients: 600 g potatoes, cut into 2 cm pieces
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the potatoes and carrots with half the oil in a large roasting tray.
Rub the chicken with the remaining oil, thyme, salt and pepper and arrange on top with the lemon slices.
Roast for 45 to 50 minutes, turning the vegetables halfway through, until tender and the chicken reaches 74°C in the thickest part, away from the bone.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes while keeping the vegetables warm, then divide among four plates.

title: Coconut Red Lentil Dal
description: Red lentils simmer with ginger, tomatoes and coconut milk for a comforting bowl of gently spiced dal.
steps: Warm the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin and turmeric and cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk, water and salt. Simmer gently for 18 to 19 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils are tender; loosen with extra water if needed.
Stir in the lime juice, taste for seasoning and serve in warmed bowls.

title: Mushroom and Pea Risotto
description: Slowly stirred rice becomes creamy with browned mushrooms, sweet peas and a little hard cheese.
ingredients: 50 g vegetarian hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Bring the stock to a gentle simmer in a separate saucepan and keep it hot.
Heat half the oil in a wide pan and fry the mushrooms for 6 minutes until browned; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and onion to the pan and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the rice for 1 minute.
Add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring and letting each addition absorb before the next, for 18 to 20 minutes until the rice is tender with a slight bite.
Stir in the peas and mushrooms with a final ladle of stock and cook for 3 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in the butter and cheese, season with pepper and rest for 2 minutes before serving.

title: Pan-Seared Salmon and Green Beans
description: Crisp-skinned salmon pairs with green beans and a quick mustard-lemon dressing.
ingredients: 2 skin-on salmon fillets, about 150 g each
steps: Pat the salmon dry and season with salt and pepper. Whisk the mustard, lemon juice and water together in a small bowl.
Boil the beans in water for 5 to 6 minutes until tender, then drain and keep warm.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Cook the salmon skin-side down for 6 to 8 minutes, then turn and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the centre reaches 63°C.
Divide the beans and salmon between two plates and spoon over the dressing.

title: Pear and Oat Crumble
description: Soft baked pears sit beneath a buttery oat topping in this cosy dessert.
ingredients: 4 ripe pears, peeled, cored and sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Toss the pears with the lemon juice and cinnamon in a small baking dish.
Rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir the oats and sugar into the crumbs and scatter evenly over the pears.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and the fruit is bubbling, then let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Dark Chocolate Mousse
description: Dark chocolate and whipped cream make a rich, egg-free mousse. Allow two hours of chilling within the preparation time before serving.
steps: Melt the chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over gently simmering water for about 5 minutes, keeping the bowl above the water; remove and cool for 10 minutes.
Whip the cream, icing sugar and vanilla in a separate bowl until soft peaks form.
Fold a spoonful of cream into the cooled chocolate, then gently fold in the remaining cream until combined.
Spoon into four small glasses and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before topping with raspberries.
